definition: A collision in which the total kinetic energy of the bodies is the same afterwards as before, as well as the total momentum; head-on, they separate at the same relative speed at which they approached.
A collision in which total momentum is conserved but the total kinetic energy decreases, because some is transferred to other forms such as internal energy and sound.
An event in which internal forces, using stored energy, push the parts of a system apart: the total momentum is conserved and the total kinetic energy increases.
